Cloud SKU Translation + Merchant Voice Copy (draft)

Purpose:
This working doc captures a recommended approach to translate Redwood product SKUs, pricing tiers, and value-copy into marketplace-ready artifacts for AWS/Azure/GCP listings — with a special focus on regulated customers (HIPAA, SOC2, EU data residency). This is an early draft: objectives are to (1) create a repeatable SKU translation matrix, (2) propose short/long copy variants in merchant tone, and (3) surface compliance and billing triggers that block approvals.

Audience:
- Internal: GTM, Finance, Legal, PartnerOps, Solutions Engineers
- External consumers: marketplace reviewers, procurement teams at regulated companies, channel partners

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- One SKU translation table per cloud that maps Redwood product SKU -> marketplace SKU -> billing metric (tokens, vCPU hours, flat seat)
- 3 copy levels per listing: tagline (6–8 words), short (1–2 sentences), long (3–5 bullets + paragraph)
- Compliance checklist that must be green before submitting (data residency, encryption, contract flow)
- Published listings with accurate pricing and linking to Dedicated/Private options (not just hosted API)

Notes / constraints:
- Marketplace listing copy should not claim specific SLAs unless we have a marketplace-plan with SLA add-on. Avoid hard commitments like "99.99% uptime" in copy unless approved by Legal.
- For regulated verticals, emphasize deployment options + encryption + KMS/HSM support and link to Private offering.
- Some clouds require monthly metering mapping (e.g., AWS meter:api.unit). Finance needs mapping before we submit.

SKU translation matrix (example rows; full table lives in spreadsheet linked above):
- Redwood-Hosted-API-Standard -> aws:rdw-hosted-standard -> billing metric: tokens_consumed_monthly -> price_map: $0.0004/token (list price placeholder)
- Redwood-Dedicated-4xA10G -> azure:rdw-dedicated-4xA10G -> billing metric: reserved_gpu_hours -> contract SKU for reserved capacity
- Redwood-Private-OnPrem -> gcp:rdw-private-onprem -> billing metric: one-time-license + annual-support

Open questions (for finance/legal):
- Do cloud marketplaces support pass-through consumption billing (tokens) or do we need to convert to hourly SKU + usage reconciliation? (JIRA-GTM-1294)
- For enterprise discounts/negotiated contracts, what does downstream invoicing look like with marketplace?

Merchant voice: copy principles
- Voice: pragmatic, developer-forward, ops-minded. Focus on predictability and economics ("predictable inference for production apps").
- Avoid deep model claims ("largest context window") unless model vendor copy is integrated.
- Call out deployment types and a single CTA path: "Get started with a free trial" -> then surface Dedicated/Private contact flow for regulated customers.

Suggested tagline variants (6–8 words):
- "Predictable, low-latency LLM inference at scale"
- "Production-ready LLM serving with predictable economics"
- "Run inference with predictable latency and cost"

Short description variants (1–2 sentences):
- Variant A (developer): "Redwood Inference provides a production-grade runtime for serving LLMs with transparent performance and cost controls — hosted, dedicated, or private deployments for regulated workloads."
- Variant B (ops/enterprise): "High-throughput inference with SLA-backed dedicated capacity and private deployments, plus tooling to minimize latency and unit cost for production ML features."

Long description / bullets (3–5 bullets + supporting paragraph):
- Bullet ideas:
  - "Unified API for text generation, embeddings, and reranking with streaming responses and function calls."
  - "Dedicated capacity options for predictable throughput and tenant isolation."
  - "Private deployment path (VPC & on-prem) with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logging for compliance."
  - "Optimize costs with caching, batching, and quantization recommendations tailored to your workload."
  - "Observability: token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency metrics, and rollout controls for safe model upgrades."

Compliance & Partner Ops checklist (must be green):
- Legal sign-off on listing copy (no SLA claims) [owner: Legal]
- Data residency statement corresponding to region listing [owner: Solutions Eng]
- KMS/HSM technical note and documentation link included [owner: Security]
- EULA/license mapping: confirm one-time vs recurring SKU definitions [owner: Finance]
- Privacy and DPA link present (with contact for executed DPA) [owner: Legal]
- Audit log / logging export notes included for forums where required [owner: Product]

Assets required for submission:
- 2–3 screenshots: Console dashboard (latency view), Deployment selector (hosted/dedicated/private), Billing page example
- 1 short explainer video (30–60s) — optional but increases listing conversions
- Logo variants (SVG, PNG 1x/2x) and short company blurb (20–30 words)

Localization guidance:
- Primary listing language = English; prioritize German and French for EU regions where we plan to sell Dedicated/Private. Copy should avoid US-centric regulatory statements for EU listings.

Acceptance criteria (before clicking submit):
- Finance has provided per-cloud SKU mapping spreadsheet and validated list prices
- Legal has approved final copy and DPA/terms links are present
- Security has validated any "compliance" statements and provided artifact links
- PartnerOps has an intake ticket for marketplace procurement team sync
- Product has reviewed screenshots and owner-approved features map

Quick rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 1: hosted API listing (low-risk copy, developer-focused, consumption billing) — target: Q1 initial submission
- Phase 2: Dedicated offering (requires reserved capacity SKUs + SLA add-on language) — target: Q2
- Phase 3: Private (VPC/on-prem) listing with procurement flow & partner contact (requires legal/finance playbook) — target: Q3

Submission blockers (hard stops):
- Missing finance SKU mapping for consumption metrics per cloud
- Copy that implies a different data-processing regime than our privacy policy
- Any marketplace contract clause that forces data to be routed through a partner without customer consent

Freeform notes / TODOs:
- Consider a dedicated "Regulated" badge on listing to quickly call out Private/Dedicated options — is this allowed by marketplaces? (ask PartnerOps)
- Evaluate whether "per-token" is a workable metering primitive on Azure Marketplace — early signs say we may need an hourly SKU wrapper
- Keep copy short and scannable; marketplace reviewers prefer clear bullets and explicit supported features (list model names only if vendor OKs it)

Slack threads / refs: 
- slack:#gtm-marketplace (thread: marketplace-sku-thread)
- slack:#legal (thread: marketplace-terms-review)

This is a working draft — leave comments inline or add items to JIRA-GTM-1294.

Last note: prioritize a minimal, accurate hosted listing first — it unlocks customer trials. Dedicated/Private require more orchestration; plan those as follow-ups rather than blocking the hosted submission.
